Subject: Request: how will service credit be apportioned after June 21 incident?

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the incident notification earlier this week. Our billing team asked me to follow up to understand how Redwood plans to allocate the service credit across our account and subaccounts. We had three active projects during the outage window (core-api, ingestion, model-training) and need a clear breakdown for our internal chargebacks.

Could you confirm:
- Which exact time window you're using for the outage calculation (your postmortem report referenced 2026-06-21 03:12–03:52 UTC — does that match what you used?)
- Whether credits are applied at the top-level account only or split pro-rata to subaccounts by token usage/dollars spent?
- An example calculation (numbers) so we can validate with our finance team.

Elena (cc) and I also need an ETA for issuance — will the credit show on the next invoice or as an immediate one-off adjustment?

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can close our internal ticket.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
VP of Engineering, Greentech Solutions

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-25T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: how will service credit be apportioned after June 21 incident?

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by the methodology and an example.

1) Time window: we are using the same window as the postmortem — 2026-06-21T03:12:00Z to 2026-06-21T03:52:00Z (40 minutes). We measured degraded throughput and elevated error rates across affected hosts in that window.

2) Allocation approach: we apply an account-level remediation credit (per the SLA) and then split it to subaccounts proportionally by billable token consumption in the 30-day billing period that contains the incident — unless you prefer allocation by last-week usage. Most customers choose the 30-day pro-rata split to smooth variance.

3) Example calculation (attached): I ran a quick pass and attached two files: sla_outage_log.csv (events we measured) and credit_calc_greentech_v1.xlsx (worked numbers). Summary: total eligible credit = 4% of June spend for the affected services window. That equates to $23,450.00 total. Using 30-day token consumption split across your three projects, the credit allocation would be: core-api $13,200; ingestion $6,900; model-training $3,350.

Issuance: we can either apply as a one-time invoice adjustment (recommended) or as a credit line on the next invoice. If you want immediate adjustment before the next billing cycle, I can route to Finance for expedited issuance — please confirm preference.

Next steps: confirm allocation method (30-day pro-rata or last-week), and whether you want immediate adjustment. Once confirmed, I'll route to Finance and Marissa will track the payout.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
